questions.q: What does a reference label add to a card visual?
options: A second, smaller supporting value shown alongside the main callout number
A drill-down hierarchy
An automatic forecast of future values
A filter that only shows values above a threshold
questions.explain: Reference labels give a bare number context — like pairing a Units count with its return rate — without needing a second visual.

questions.q: What does a KPI visual add beyond a plain card?
options: It automatically applies conditional formatting
It can display more than one measure, while a card can only show one
It can only be used in the Power BI service, not Desktop
It shows progress toward a specific, measurable target, not just the value itself
questions.explain: A card answers 'what is this value.' A KPI visual answers 'how close is this value to its goal' by tracking progress toward a defined target.

questions.q: What's a key advantage of a slicer over the Filters pane?
options: The Filters pane can only filter one visual at a time
A slicer is always visible on the canvas, making the current filter state obvious at a glance
Slicers can filter data that the Filters pane cannot
Slicers work only in the Power BI service
questions.explain: The Filters pane is hidden until opened; a slicer sits directly on the canvas, showing viewers exactly what's currently selected.

questions.q: When Select all is enabled on a slicer and a viewer clears one item, what filter does Power BI actually apply?
options: The slicer becomes permanently disabled
No filter is applied at all
An "is not" filter containing only the cleared item, rather than an "is" filter listing every remaining value
A filter that excludes every value, including the ones still shown as selected
questions.explain: This inverted-selection behavior means new values added later (e.g. after a refresh) are automatically included, since nothing explicitly excluded them.

questions.q: Which slicer type is best suited for large datasets where users need to search or navigate a hierarchy?
options: Button slicer
Input slicer
List slicer
Card visual
questions.explain: The List slicer is designed for large datasets, offering search functionality and hierarchical navigation that a simple button or dropdown slicer doesn't provide.
